item: A runtime ratchet drives every GET operation with the kill switch engaged and accounts for each socket, thread, file and write statement (audit 0.5.0 item 35 follow-on, P3)
refs: PR #1533; coordinator 27 Oct 00:21: R278, P3 runtime ratchet, floor 467, kill switch engaged, under about 2 min; audit-0.5.0/get-side-effects-2026-10-27.md
summary: tests/test_get_routes_side_effects.py drives every GET operation of the app's OpenAPI schema (467 on the full install, 464 Core-only) plus five hidden GETs pinned to the source (/favicon.ico, /unlock, /desk, /static/oo.js, /metrics/) once (about 40 s) with the network kill switch engaged, while monitors record socket connect, connect_ex and sendto and DNS lookups through getaddrinfo, gethostbyname and gethostbyname_ex (blocked and recorded), threads started (the rate limiter's own expiry timer is not counted), files created, changed or removed under the data directories, write statements through the engine (including WITH ... DELETE, comment-prefixed statements and PRAGMA x = y) and any change to the main database file seen from a second connection (PRAGMA data_version, which also catches a raw sqlite3 write). Asserts: no GET reaches a non-loopback address; only the llm/* and diagnostics model routes open a loopback socket; every thread and file is in an ambient table or in a per-route table whose entries carry the reason or the finding (F1 heavy diagnostics GETs, F2 signing keys minted by custody/annotations export, both routed to RC2 by R278); no GET issues a write statement or changes the database file; no GET answers 5xx (the walk does not re-raise, so a raising handler is named). Monitor liveness is pinned for every patched call (with the switch cleared /api/hazards is seen looking up usgs and gdacs). RED-WITHOUT shown: a mutant GET that starts a thread, writes a file and connects to 93.184.216.34 fails two tests naming the route. Folded from the Opus read: a warm-up request and ambient rows for the error log's lock file and the crash black box, so the result no longer depends on which tests ran before (it failed after any DB-seeding file); the floors state both install profiles (R283). Limits stated in the docstring: the suite's shared database, whatever earlier tests left in it; the 74 routes that answer 4xx never reach their handler body; a file created and removed within one request (GET /api/database/backup's snapshot.db, which has its own cross-site guard, R214) is not seen; effects are attributed by time window so a background writer lands on a later route; allowances match a basename anywhere and a thread by name. On main after #1526 the six FINDING routes refuse a cross-site request, pinned route by route (the measured effect stays listed, since a same-origin call still causes it). Folded from the delta read: atomic-write temp names as the app's temp_name() produces them (<name>.tmp.<pid>.<thread>), the write classifier built on the repo's own is_plain_read allow-list (VACUUM INTO, REINDEX, ATTACH, wal_checkpoint, PRAGMA x(v) are writes), and programs started by a GET recorded through Popen, os.system and os.posix_spawn (only nvidia-smi, uname and xdg-user-dir are listed, each a local query).
